messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to lock down the private/VPC routing policy for sandbox tenants. Constraints: strict egress, allowed regions only, and a clear model-variant fallback order. Also need telemetry shape for console. Thoughts?

jon: +1. My reading: control plane calls (billing, rollouts) can hit our CP endpoints, but inference egress out of the tenant VPC must be blocked unless explicitly allowed. That implies two things: 1) policy language to express allowed upstream regions/endpoints, 2) a fallback semantics when preferred model variant is unavailable.

sasha: Security note: telemetry that crosses control plane must be minimized and scrubbed. No raw client IPs or customer data should come back to hosted console by default. We need a data-classification toggle per tenant.

kevin: On fallback: we should encode preference for variant family -> quantization -> hosted/dedicated tier. Example fallback order: preferred (dedicated quantized) -> hosted fp16 -> reject. Important to expose cost delta in the console when a fallback happens.

lina: UX: for rollouts we need an explicit "fallback policy" card in the Private tenant UI that shows current priority list and a quick "reject traffic" button. Also telemetry panels: recent fallback counts, latency delta, tokens spilled to hosted.

jon: Draft policy example (will need schema iteration):
```json
{
  "allow_regions": ["us-west-2", "eu-central-1"],
  "egress_mode": "blocked", // blocked | limited | open
  "control_plane_endpoints": ["cp.redwood-internal.example"],
  "fallback_policy": [
    {"priority": 1, "model": "redwood/llama2-13b-q8", "tier": "dedicated"},
    {"priority": 2, "model": "open/llama2-13b-fp16", "tier": "hosted-lower"},
    {"priority": 3, "action": "reject"}
  ]
}
```

maria: That looks good. A couple of edge cases: what if the allowed_regions list excludes a region required by the hosted fallback? We should make fallback aware of region compatibility and surface an explicit "cross-region fallback" consent in the tenant settings.

sasha: Agreed. Default should be deny cross-region compute. Tenant can opt-in (and sign an SLA addendum) for cross-region hosting. Also telemetry must log only the fallback *event* and the model id, not full request payloads.

kevin: Also quota implications: when fallback goes to hosted we need per-tenant meter tagging and quota enforcement so customers are billed or charged against a separate emergency bucket. Proposal: default private quota = 5_000_000 tokens/month with an emergency hosted buffer of 50_000 tokens; any use beyond buffer must be explicitly approved or auto-rejected.

lina: Console mocks: show current token spend, fallback-breakdowns (counts, tokens, avg latency), and a toggle for auto-fallback vs manual approval. If manual, send a rollup notification to owners.

maria: For control-plane API design we need two endpoints: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/routing-policy (upsert) and GET /v1/tenants/{id}/routing-policy/eval which returns an evaluated decision for a given request context. Internal example:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/llama2-13b-q8","region":"us-east-1"}' \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/123/routing-policy/eval
```

jon: Implementation note: eval should be deterministic and cacheable. We can compute a policy fingerprint and cache for 5m per-tenant. Telemetry should emit policy_fingerprint + decision + reason. Decision reasons: "preferred_available", "region_blocked", "variant_unavailable", "quota_exhausted", "opted_out_cross_region".

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: feature/priv-routing-eval -> staging at 2026-03-18T14:20Z :rocket:

kevin: One more: fallback to hosted must never silently downgrade accuracy without notice. Add a quality-tag on each variant (e.g., "quality: 0.92") and surface in telemetry and alerts when fallback reduces quality beyond threshold.

sasha: Ops/security: add audit log entries for any change to routing-policy and for every evaluated decision that results in cross-region egress. Retention 1 year by default for enterprise tenants.

lina: UX followups: create a small badge in tenant list that shows "routing policy status" (green/yellow/red) and clicking opens the detailed fallback timeline.

maria: Action items: @jon to draft API schema & evaluation semantics, @sasha to write telemetry privacy checklist, @kevin to propose default fallback lists per model family, @lina to mock the UI card. Let's sync next Thurs 10am.

jon: I'll ship a PoC eval service and JSON schema by Wednesday EOD.

sasha: I'll draft the privacy checklist and list of prohibited telemetry fields.

kevin: Will compile model-family fallback suggestions and a small script to estimate cost delta for hosted fallbacks.

lina: I'll add the UI card to the design board and start wireframes.

maria: Thanks folks. If anyone wants to play with the policy simulator, here's a quick curl to test eval (staging):

`curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING" -d '{"model":"redwood/llama2-13b-q8","seq_len":512,"region":"eu-central-1"}' https://staging-controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/demo/routing-policy/eval | jq`

lina: :eyes: love the simulator idea.

kevin: :thumbsup:

sasha: :lock: I'll add the telemetry gating to the checklist.

maria: Closing thread, we'll capture notes in the eng-platform RFC repo.
